name: Kneeling Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
description: The kneeling single-arm lat pulldown removes leg drive and hip momentum by placing the lifter in a tall kneeling position, while the unilateral arm action allows independent lat development. The kneeling position also engages the core and hip flexors for stability, and the single-arm pull allows the working-side shoulder to fully protract and retract throughout the range of motion.

execution.starting_position: Kneel upright facing a cable machine. Attach a single handle at the highest position. Grip with one hand, arm extended overhead.
execution.setup_instructions: Kneel on a mat or pad for comfort. Place the kneeling position far enough from the cable to allow full arm extension overhead.
steps: Step 1: Kneel tall — hips extended, torso upright.
Step 2: Reach the working arm fully overhead.
Step 3: Pull the handle down and toward the working-side hip by driving the elbow down.
Step 5: Return to full overhead extension. Complete all reps then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale returning to full extension.
common_mistakes: Hips flexing (sitting back) during the pull — maintain upright kneeling
Leaning back to assist — stay tall and let the lat do the work
safety_considerations: Kneel on a padded surface to protect the knees
Do not load beyond what allows perfect upright posture
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead extension to elbow at or below shoulder level.
coaching_cues: Hips tall — do not sit back
Drive the elbow to the hip
Full reach at the top of every rep
